youtube_title: Barker Mansion, Michigan City: the 14-year-old who inherited a freight car fortune
body: In 1910, a 14-year-old girl in Michigan City lost both of her parents, and she inherited a freight car fortune. Her name was Catherine Barker. Her father, John H. Barker, ran the Haskell and Barker Car Company, one of the biggest freight car builders in the country, and he turned the family home on Washington Street into a 38-room mansion. Then, in 1910, Catherine's mother died, and before the year was out, her father died too. Newspapers put her inheritance in the millions. She grew up to start a foundation that still carries the family name. In 1968, the mansion was given to the people of Michigan City. It's now a museum you can tour, May through December.
